solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Unusually brilliant choice, wouldn’t you agree? (11)

blocks.note: choice as an adjective: excellent, top quality
a tag asking for agreement: 'right?'

annotation.surface: Someone praises an inspired pick and fishes for agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: "Choice" reads as a noun, a decision, but it is the adjective meaning excellent; the question tag is spoken English for RIGHT?
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the prefix super- intensifies, so something super-bright shines far beyond the ordinary.

entries.clue: Exhaust an army engineer (6)

blocks.note: to sap is to drain or exhaust
an as in 'ten pounds an hour', meaning per

annotation.surface: Something wears out a military engineer.
annotation.walkthrough: The little word "an" does real work: 'a pound an hour' means a pound per hour.
annotation.definitionFit: British military term: sappers are soldiers of the Royal Engineers, named from digging saps, or trenches.

entries.clue: Doorman full of characteristic anguish faces renderer (8,7)

indicatorNotes.full of: a doorman full of something has it packed inside him, so PORTER holds the next two pieces

blocks.note: a porter minds the door
a trait is a characteristic
pain is anguish

annotation.surface: A doorman, full of his usual angst, confronts a renderer.
annotation.walkthrough: "Faces" looks like a verb, confronting someone, but it is the object of "renderer": one who renders faces.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: to render is to depict in paint, and a portrait painter's subject is people's faces.

entries.clue: Novel handcuff inverted for jails (5,1,4)

indicatorNotes.inverted: inverted means turned upside down, and in a down entry that flips FOR to ROF
indicatorNotes.jails: to jail is to lock up, so ROF locks MANACLE inside it

blocks.note: FOR turned over
a manacle is a handcuff or shackle

annotation.surface: A strange handcuff, fitted upside down, used in prisons.
annotation.walkthrough: "Novel" poses as an adjective, new, describing the handcuff; it is the noun and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: French term used in English: a roman à clef, 'novel with a key', portrays real people under invented names.

entries.clue: Assess fifth man involved with Burgess, Maclean, etc.? (4)

blocks.clueFragment: man involved with Burgess, Maclean, etc.?
blocks.note: Burgess and Maclean were Cambridge spies who betrayed their country, and a traitor is a rat
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone sizes up the 'fifth man' of the Cambridge spy ring.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cambridge Five were British spies for the Soviet Union, and the hunt for their 'fifth man' was long famous; here the fifth is only the letter E.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to rate a thing is to judge its value, as a critic rates a film.

entries.clue: Dinner cooked in silence, tending to pots etc (9)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooked as in cooked books: tampered with, so DINNER's letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: in places the rearranged letters inside GAG

blocks.note: to gag someone is to silence them
anagram of DINNER

annotation.surface: Someone cooks dinner without a word, minding the pots and pans.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes "pots" saucepans; the definition means flowerpots.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: looking after potted plants, beds and borders is what gardening involves.

entries.clue: Wait, Spooner’s identifying graffito in green (4,3)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so his version of the phrase trades their fronts

blocks.note: lime is a shade of green; it trades its L for the T of the next word
a tag is a graffiti artist's signature; it takes the L

annotation.surface: Spooner stops to point out a scrawl of graffiti in green paint.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase to swap is 'lime tag', a green graffiti signature.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a time lag is the interval you wait between one event and its consequence.

entries.clue: African wastes time and Serb jitters (5,6)

indicatorNotes.jitters: letters with the jitters shake nervously out of place into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: An African man wastes time while a Serb has the jitters.
annotation.walkthrough: "African wastes" reads as a man wasting something; wastes is the noun, a wilderness.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: wastes are barren wilds, and the Namib is a coastal desert in south-west Africa.

entries.clue: Add points after German’s cry of disbelief heard — 180! (9)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is only the sound, so NEIN may be spelt as the number NINE

blocks.note: nein is German for no
to score is to add points

annotation.surface: A darts crowd: a German can't believe it when a 180 goes up on the board.
annotation.walkthrough: 180 is the maximum in darts, so the surface is a match; the answer does the sum instead: nine twenties.
annotation.definitionFit: Arithmetic: a score is twenty, so nine score is nine twenties, 180.

entries.clue: Ersatz feature of Weimar Germany (5)

annotation.definitionNote: Ersatz here is the noun: a substitute

indicatorNotes.feature of: a feature of something is part of it, so the answer is a part inside the following words

blocks.note: weiMAR GErmany

annotation.surface: A remark that substitutes were typical of Weimar Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: Ersatz is a German word, which suits the surface; marge is British shorthand for margarine.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: margarine is the classic ersatz butter, a cheap substitute.

entries.clue: Rubbish smelled round at the end (4-5)

blocks.note: bull is slang for nonsense
to nose is to smell out

annotation.surface: Someone sniffed around the rubbish near the end.
annotation.walkthrough: "Round" pairs with "smelled" to suggest sniffing about; it is the adjective in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical term: bricks, steps and vehicles are called bull-nosed when their front end is rounded like a bull's snout.

entries.clue: Exile restored art in atonement (12)

indicatorNotes.restored: restored means rebuilt, so ART is put back together in a new order
indicatorNotes.in: in places the rebuilt letters inside EXPIATION

blocks.note: expiation is atonement for a wrong
anagram of ART

annotation.surface: An exiled work of art is returned as a gesture of atonement.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is looted art being repatriated; "restored" means rearranged, not repaired.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: expatriation is living outside one's own country, whether banished or by choice.

entries.clue: European agreed product of mine’s a blight (7)

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation of European
yes signals agreement
ore is what a mine produces

annotation.surface: Europeans agree that the output of a mine is a blot on the landscape.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mine’s" reads as mine is: the product of the mine is a blight.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a blight on the landscape is something ugly that spoils the view.

entries.clue: Temperature strains rails (6)

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation of temperature
to rack is to strain or torment

annotation.surface: Heat puts rails under strain, buckling them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a summer railway problem, which is why the plain definition hides so well.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: railway track is made of the steel rails trains run on.

entries.clue: Outside frost, inside safe (9)

annotation.definitionNote: Outside here is the noun: the outer edge

indicatorNotes.inside: inside says where one thing sits within another: RIME within PETER

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
rime is hoar frost

annotation.surface: Frost outdoors, but safe and sound indoors.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter for a safe is old criminal slang, familiar from safe-crackers (peter men).
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense: the outside of an area, its boundary line, is its perimeter.

entries.clue: Cross if mushroom sandwiches no good (7)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so MOREL holds NG in the middle

blocks.note: the morel is an edible mushroom
NG is the abbreviation of no good

annotation.surface: Someone is annoyed that their mushroom sandwiches are no good.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cross" reads as angry; it is the noun, a crossbreed.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a cross is an animal of mixed breeding, and a mongrel is a dog of that kind.

entries.clue: Detective consumed about miserable work Mary’s in (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about as in turned about, facing the other way, so ATE runs backwards

blocks.note: PI is a private investigator
ATE, consumed, turned round

annotation.surface: A detective gorged on something while grumbling about a job Mary is involved in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Miserable work" sounds like a dreary job; it is a grieving artwork, and Mary is the Virgin.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a pietà is a sorrowful artwork showing the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

entries.clue: Misbehave with job you have to travel for (6)

annotation.definition: job you have to travel for

blocks.note: to err is to go wrong, stray from good conduct
with and and both join things

annotation.surface: Someone misbehaves on a work trip.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a business trip; the definition is just a short outing to get something done.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: an errand is a task that takes you out somewhere, like fetching milk.

entries.clue: Having lost social standing last month, girl back in disgrace (8)

indicatorNotes.back in: the back of a word is its end, so this takes the last letter in disgrace

blocks.note: December is the last month of the year
a lass is a girl
last letter of disgrace

annotation.surface: A girl, disgraced last month, has slipped down the social ladder.
annotation.walkthrough: "Last month" looks like a time phrase in the story; it is the month of the year that comes last.
annotation.definitionFit: French borrowing: déclassé literally means 'declassed', fallen out of one's social class.

entries.clue: Complicated system where J seats are switched round with K (7)

indicatorNotes.switched round: switched round means turned to face the other way, so ROW TEN reads backwards

blocks.clueFragment: where J seats are switched round
blocks.note: seats lettered J are in the tenth row, since J is the tenth letter; ROW TEN reversed
K added at the end

annotation.surface: A seating plan where the J and K seats have been swapped.
annotation.walkthrough: "Switched round with K" suggests swapping J for K; K is simply added. J is the tenth letter, so its seats are in row ten.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a network is an intricate system of interconnected lines or parts.

entries.clue: Pure E dropped by minister at home (8)

indicatorNotes.dropped: in a down entry, something dropped falls lower, so the E falls from PRIEST to the foot of the answer

blocks.note: a priest is a minister of religion
PRIEST with its E taken out
in means at home
the E, dropped to the foot of the entry

annotation.surface: A minister at home drops the drug Ecstasy, keeping himself pure.
annotation.walkthrough: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy in the surface; in the wordplay the letter E falls from inside PRIEST to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: pristine means untouched and unspoilt, in its pure original state.

entries.clue: Delivery of sauce in fog and frost, bad decision (11,2,7)

indicatorNotes.in: in places the first phrase inside MIST

blocks.note: mist is thin fog
carriage is conveyance, delivery of goods
taken as it stands
jus is a thin gravy or sauce
frost is ice

annotation.surface: A sauce delivery is caught in fog and frost, a poor call by someone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Delivery" hints at childbirth to set up MISCARRIAGE, but it is carriage, as in carriage paid.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal idiom: a miscarriage of justice is a court's wrong verdict, the worst kind of bad decision.

entries.clue: American coffee cups and English crackers for DA’s party? (4,3)

indicatorNotes.cups: to cup something is to hold it in cupped hands, so JOE holds the rest
indicatorNotes.crackers: crackers means crazy, so AND E go wild and change order

blocks.note: joe is US slang for coffee
anagram of AND + E (English)

annotation.surface: A party for a district attorney with American coffee and English Christmas crackers.
annotation.walkthrough: "Party" suggests a celebration; it is a party in a lawsuit, as a DA (US district attorney) would use the word.
annotation.definitionFit: US legal usage: Jane Doe is the placeholder name for an unidentified woman who is a party to a case.

entries.clue: Very little money in bank of late (8)

blocks.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a tiny sum

annotation.surface: Lately there has been almost no money in the bank.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bank" is the verb, as in bank on someone, not a place for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'of late' and recently both mean in the period just past.

entries.clue: Eg Victoria train that’s fast making ten miles (7)

indicatorNotes.making: making means turning into, so the ten becomes miles: X turns into M

blocks.note: an express is a fast train
X is the Roman numeral for ten
M is the abbreviation of miles

annotation.surface: A train from Victoria station goes ten miles fast.
annotation.walkthrough: Victoria is a London terminus, so trains fit; here she is Queen Victoria.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Queen Victoria also held the title Empress of India.

entries.clue: Quotation I didn’t understand that includes meat charge (8)

indicatorNotes.includes: a word that includes others has them within it, so EH holds the other two

blocks.note: eh? is what you say when you haven't followed
pig as the meat, pork
a rap is a criminal charge

annotation.surface: Someone baffled by a quote on a butcher's bill.
annotation.walkthrough: "Charge" sounds like a price to go with the meat; it is a rap, a criminal charge.
annotation.definitionFit: Specific sense: an epigraph is a short quotation set at the head of a book or chapter.

entries.clue: Ship originally named after young female lion (7)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of named is used
indicatorNotes.after: after says the N comes behind the other pieces

blocks.note: gal is a girl
Leo is the lion of the zodiac
first letter of named

annotation.surface: A ship first named after a lioness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a ship being christened; "after" is not 'in honour of' but a placement word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a galleon is a large square-rigged sailing ship of the 16th and 17th centuries.

entries.clue: Fish rising check worm in the water (5)

indicatorNotes.rising: rising means going up, and in a down entry EEL reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: EEL, a fish, turned upwards
CH is the chess notation for check

annotation.surface: A rising fish checks on a worm in the water, as if about to eat it.
annotation.walkthrough: A leech counts as a worm: it is a segmented worm, even though it looks unlike an earthworm.
annotation.definitionFit: Zoological class: leeches are annelid worms, most of which live in fresh water.

entries.clue: Useful information mostly wasted, good to see (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so BLEW loses its last letter

blocks.note: data is information
to blow money is to waste it
BLEW minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Useful information was mostly wasted, but good to see anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: "Good to see" means worth going out with, as in dating, not pleasant to look at.
annotation.definitionFit: Dating sense: to see someone is to go out with them, and a datable person is suitable for that.

entries.clue: Poet holds aces, cards to go all in (4,4,7)

indicatorNotes.holds: a poet who holds something grips it inside, so BURNS holds ONE

blocks.note: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet
an ace counts as one
bridge is a card game; games of bridge

annotation.surface: A poet at a poker table with aces goes all in.
annotation.walkthrough: The poker picture makes "go all in" a bet; it means commit with no way back.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: burning your bridges leaves no retreat, so you are fully committed, as a poker player going all in is.

entries.clue: Flag one gets up shortly (4)

indicatorNotes.shortly: shortly means in short form, so RISES is cut down

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rises means gets up
RISES shortened to its first three letters

annotation.surface: A flag goes up in a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flag" suggests a banner being raised; it is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Botanical name: flag is an old name for the iris, especially the yellow flag of riverbanks.

entries.clue: Still having had no success pinching diamonds (8)

indicatorNotes.pinching: to pinch is to grip between fingers, so WINLESS grips D inside it

blocks.note: without a win
D is the abbreviation of diamonds in cards

annotation.surface: A failed jewel thief still has not managed to steal the diamonds.
annotation.walkthrough: "Still" reads as 'even now'; it is the adjective, calm.
annotation.definitionFit: Weather sense: still air is air with no wind moving.

entries.clue: Make useless treatment for baldies (7)

indicatorNotes.treatment for: treatment works something over, so BALDIES is processed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A useless hair-restoring treatment for bald men.
annotation.walkthrough: "Make useless" seems to judge the treatment; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to disable a machine is to stop it working, making it useless.

entries.clue: Time for training group’s last weight-lifting exercise (5)

indicatorNotes.for: for as in 'in exchange for', so T replaces the last letter

blocks.note: a squad trains together
the last letter of SQUAD
T is the abbreviation of time

annotation.surface: It is time for the training group's final lift.
annotation.walkthrough: "Time for training" reads as a gym call; it is T replacing the last letter of the squad.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the squat, bending the knees under a loaded bar, is a standard weight-lifting exercise.

entries.clue: Record what we have first in each debate (9)

indicatorNotes.first in: the first letter in each word, here the single word each

blocks.note: a record is a disc
what we have is ours
first letter of each

annotation.surface: A plea to log what we have first in every debate.
annotation.walkthrough: "Record" looks like a verb, to note down; it is the noun, a disc.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: discourse is formal discussion or debate on a subject.

entries.clue: Every so often sup ale and express spit (8)

indicatorNotes.Every so often: every so often means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: odd letters of sup ale: S, P, L
to utter is to express

annotation.surface: Someone drinking beer occasionally spits it out.
annotation.walkthrough: "Express" reads as quick; it is the verb, to say out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to splutter is to spit out drink or words in a noisy burst.

entries.clue: Southern Spain’s English diner fitting one in on trip (6-6)

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation of southern
inglés is Spanish for English
a diner is an eater

annotation.surface: An English diner in southern Spain squeezes a meal into their trip.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a holiday meal; the definition describes a vehicle that takes only one person.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a single-seater car or plane has room for one person on a journey.

entries.clue: Bad condition of train set upset son (9)

indicatorNotes.upset: upset means knocked over, so TRAIN SET tips into a new order

blocks.note: anagram of TRAIN SET
S is the abbreviation of son

annotation.surface: A boy is upset at the poor state of his train set.
annotation.walkthrough: Ratty is British informal for irritable, so the bad condition is a bad temper.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British sense: rattiness is irritability, a bad-tempered state of mind.

entries.clue: Apply force, breaking church’s buzzer in the vicarage? (8)

indicatorNotes.breaking: to break into something is to get inside it, so USE F breaks into HOLY

blocks.note: to apply is to use
F is the symbol for force
holy: of the church

annotation.surface: Someone forces their way into a church's doorbell at the vicarage.
annotation.walkthrough: A vicarage is a vicar's house, so a buzzer there is a house fly; "buzzer" sounds like a doorbell.
annotation.definitionFit: Punning description: a housefly buzzes, and the vicarage is a house.

entries.clue: Left much room at the top? (4)

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation of left
much as in 'do you go there much?', meaning often, oft

annotation.surface: Someone left a lot of space at the top of the page.
annotation.walkthrough: "Room at the top" sounds like spare space, or the novel about social climbing; it is a room under the roof.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal reading: a loft is the room at the top of a house, under the roof.

entries.clue: Cold bottom familiar to penguins? (10)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a chilly backside; the setter means the frozen land at the bottom of the globe as maps are drawn
the question mark flags the joke: penguins know that frozen southern continent as home

annotation.surface: A penguin knows all about a chilly behind.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cold bottom" reads as a chilly backside; it is the continent at the bottom of the map.
annotation.definitionFit: Geography: on a conventional map the frozen southern continent sits at the bottom, and penguins live there.

entries.clue: Model soldier left unfinished (7)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: unfinished means lacking its end, so GONE loses its last letter

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
left means gone away
GONE minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A toy soldier left half-painted.
annotation.walkthrough: "Model soldier" reads as a toy figure; model is the definition, a perfect example.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a model of virtue is a paragon, a perfect example to copy.

entries.clue: Name of French department on holiday sounds theatrical (6,3)

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation of name
of the Oise, a French department: Oise's
off work means on holiday

annotation.surface: The name of a French department sounds grand, as if someone were on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The Oise is a department north of Paris; "of" turns it possessive. "Sounds" is the noun in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Stage direction: noises off are sound effects made offstage in a theatre.

entries.clue: Work of art, bun and book in lucky dip (4,3)

indicatorNotes.Work of: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: ART + BUN + B (book), anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A painting, a bun and a book as prizes in a lucky dip.
annotation.walkthrough: "Work of art" looks like one phrase; "Work of" is the anagram signal and art is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: British fairground game: a bran tub is a lucky dip, prizes buried in bran for children to fish out.

entries.clue: Playing cards once part of degree (9)

indicatorNotes.Playing: playing cards are shuffled, and the letters are shuffled likewise

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone once played cards for a college degree.
annotation.walkthrough: "Degree" suggests a university qualification; it is a unit of angle.
annotation.definitionFit: Unit of angle: a degree divides into sixty minutes of arc, each of sixty seconds, so this is one small part of it.

entries.clue: Cook’s richer, although dog wants a run (9)

indicatorNotes.wants: wants in the old sense of lacks, so TERRIER is short of one R

blocks.note: but and although both concede
a terrier is a dog
R is the cricket abbreviation of run
TERRIER without one R

annotation.surface: A cook's dish is richer, though the dog wants a walk.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wants" reads as desires; it means lacks.
annotation.definitionFit: Kitchen sense: in cooking, adding more butter makes a dish richer.

entries.clue: Skin treatment works like 6d? (7)

blocks.note: 6d is sixpence in old British money, and a sixpence was nicknamed this
the suffix that makes an adjective meaning 'like', as in silky

annotation.surface: A tannery works just like the entry at 6 down.
annotation.walkthrough: "6d" looks like a cross-reference to 6 down; it is six old pence, which the British called a tanner.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a tannery is works where animal skins are treated to make leather.

entries.clue: Film … hence those bleats misplaced? (3,7,2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.misplaced: misplaced means put in the wrong place, so every letter moves

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 20 letters, including the definition word

annotation.surface: A film is why the sheep's bleats have gone missing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Film" does double duty: it is the definition and four letters of the fodder. Lambs with their bleats gone are indeed silent.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: The Silence of the Lambs is the 1991 thriller film starring Jodie Foster.

entries.clue: Fever one had after hospital admitted to mistake (7)

indicatorNotes.admitted to: a patient admitted to a ward goes inside it, so H goes inside TYPO

blocks.note: a typo is a typing mistake
H is the abbreviation of hospital
I'd, I had

annotation.surface: A patient with fever was admitted to hospital by mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: The hospital picture fits the fever so well that "hospital" hides as a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: typhoid is a bacterial disease whose chief symptom is a high fever.

entries.clue: Better not a secret operation (7)

blocks.note: overt means open, not secret
op is short for operation

annotation.surface: It would be better not to run a secret operation.
annotation.walkthrough: "Better" reads as advice; it is the verb, to surpass.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to better something is to outdo it, and to overtop is to rise above it.

entries.clue: Very quickly come to a halt again when cycling? (6)

indicatorNotes.when cycling: cycling means going round, so the last letter rides round to the front

blocks.note: re-stop: stop again; its final P then moves to the front

annotation.surface: A cyclist speeds along and keeps having to stop.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cycling" suggests bikes; it means letters rotating round.
annotation.definitionFit: Musical term: presto is the Italian tempo marking for very fast.

entries.clue: Electrician informally employed in M&S (6)

blocks.note: a trade nickname: electricians are named for what flies off live wires
Marks & Spencer, the British store, has a jokey rhyming nickname whose second word is the answer

annotation.surface: An electrician works at Marks & Spencer.
annotation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street store known informally as Marks & Sparks.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for an electrician, and the second word of Marks & Sparks.

entries.clue: Agent taken by tenant back to house stuffed full (7)

indicatorNotes.back to: the back of a word is its end, so this takes the last letter of house

blocks.note: a rep, representative, is an agent
a let is a property rented out, which a tenant takes
last letter of house

annotation.surface: An agent arranges for a tenant to move back into a house full of stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: The letting-agent picture is apt: the let is what the tenant takes on.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: replete means filled to capacity, especially with food.

entries.clue: “Airline reeked” snarled tour guide (8)

indicatorNotes.snarled: snarled as in snarled up, tangled, so REEKED's letters knot into a new order

blocks.note: BA is British Airways
anagram of REEKED

annotation.surface: A tour guide growls that the airline stank.
annotation.walkthrough: "Snarled" is the guide's angry tone; it means tangled.
annotation.definitionFit: Eponym: Baedeker guidebooks, from the German publisher Karl Baedeker, became a byword for travel guides.

entries.clue: Rotation of globe stopped by Virginia, a remarkable feat! (5)

annotation.definitionNote: BRAVO is the cry greeting a remarkable feat

indicatorNotes.Rotation of: a rotation turns a thing right round, so the assembled word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.stopped by: a pipe stopped by a cork has it plugged inside, so ORB has VA in its middle

blocks.note: an orb is a globe
VA is the abbreviation of Virginia

annotation.surface: A spinning globe halted at Virginia: what a feat!
annotation.walkthrough: OVARB is built first, then the whole is rotated to give the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Exclamation: 'Bravo!' is what an audience shouts to hail a remarkable feat.

entries.clue: Live cheaply putting millions into shares (6)

indicatorNotes.putting: putting says the M is being placed somewhere
indicatorNotes.into: into names where it goes: inside SCRIP

blocks.note: scrip is share certificates
M is the abbreviation of millions

annotation.surface: Someone lives frugally so as to put millions into shares.
annotation.walkthrough: Scrip is a financial term for shares or share certificates.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to scrimp is to economise hard, as in 'scrimp and save'.

entries.clue: Letters covered by stamps — is postage going up? (4)

indicatorNotes.covered by: covered by means lying underneath, so the letters lie hidden under the words
indicatorNotes.going up: in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom, so the hidden run is reversed

blocks.note: stampS IS Postage

annotation.surface: Letters bearing stamps: is the price of postage rising again?
annotation.walkthrough: "Letters" sounds like mail to go with stamps; it means letters of the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Greek alphabet: psi is the 23rd Greek letter, written ψ; the plural is formed in the ordinary way.

entries.clue: Cry in silence? Not an option (5)

blocks.note: sh! calls for silence
something ruled out is not an option

annotation.surface: Is crying quietly off the table?
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks about weeping silently; "Cry" means call out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the call-out sense of cry, not the weeping sense the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Inferior gold ring quickly pinches (2,1,4)

indicatorNotes.pinches: to pinch is to grip between finger and thumb, so FAST grips OR inside it

blocks.note: a ring is O-shaped
fast means quickly
or is gold in heraldry

annotation.surface: Someone swiftly pockets a poor-quality gold ring.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pinches" reads as stealing in the surface; in the wordplay it means gripping, as in pinching between fingers.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: calling something a meal of a sort damns it as a poor, inferior example.

entries.clue: Ball died, dropped by rackets player up the line (9)

indicatorNotes.dropped by: something dropped by a group is left out of it, so DINS loses D

blocks.note: a din is a racket, a loud noise
DINS losing D, the abbreviation of died
a winger plays up along the touchline

annotation.surface: A rackets player died on the ball, up the line.
annotation.walkthrough: Rackets is a real racquet sport, which suits "Ball", but here it means noises.
annotation.definitionFit: Sports term: an inswinger is a ball, bowled or crossed, that curves in towards its target.

entries.clue: Model T maybe getting Tesla service inside test centre? (3,8)

indicatorNotes.inside: inside says where the service goes: within the old car

blocks.note: the Model T is an old Ford car
T is the symbol for the tesla, a unit
the RAF is one of the armed services

annotation.surface: An old Model T gets a service from Tesla at an MOT test centre.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla evokes the car maker, fitting the car picture; it is the unit. Old Trafford in Manchester is a Test cricket ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Cricket pun: Test matches are international cricket games, and Old Trafford is one of the grounds that stages them.

entries.clue: Little sister on potty lets rip a bowel movement (11)

indicatorNotes.potty: potty is British slang for crazy, so LETS RIP A goes wild and changes order
indicatorNotes.on: on means placed after, so SIS follows the rest

blocks.note: anagram of LETS RIP A
sis is short for sister

annotation.surface: A little sister on the potty lets rip.
annotation.walkthrough: "Potty" is the child's toilet in the surface and 'mad' in the wordplay; "bowel movement" is taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal medical sense: peristalsis is the wave of muscle contractions that moves food through the bowel.
